title: Nepal to get vaccination support worth Rs 8.59 billion under GAVI - The Rising Nepal
description: Nepal to get vaccination support worth Rs 8.59 billion under GAVI  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Oct 27: Nepal is to receive vaccination support worth Rs 8.59 billion till 2030 under the Global Alliance for Vaccine and Immunisation (GAVI).

The support is to be secured on the initiation of Ministry of Health and Food Safety to implement its national regular vaccination programme.

Similarly, 308,271 US Dollar that Nepal was supposed to refund due to 'errors' in the auditing of GAVI support fund it received implementation of the regular vaccination programmes from 2016-17 to 2021- 2022 is to be waived off.

The Secretariat of the line Minister described such development as a significant accomplishment.

According to the Ministry, the GAVI support plays a significant role in sustaining the vaccination programme, increasing its coverage and retaining its effectiveness. (RSS)

title: Nepal gives 35 days to agency owners yet to respond to arrest warrants - The Kathmandu Post
description: Nepal gives 35 days to agency owners yet to respond to arrest warrants  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Nepal’s Department of Foreign Employment has given people who have yet to respond to arrest warrants in foreign employment-related cases 35 days to contact the authorities, warning that their bank accounts and travel could be restricted if they fail to appear. The notice comes as the department investigates Malaysia’s selection of 25 Nepali recruitment agencies to recruit workers for the country.

The department had obtained authorisation from the Foreign Employment Tribunal to issue arrest warrants against the owners of the 25 agencies so it could question them in connection with the selection process. One of the agency owners, Rabin Gurung, has been taken into custody.

In a notice issued on Monday, the department called on those who had failed to respond to previously issued arrest warrants in foreign employment-related cases to contact the department or Nepal Police within 35 days of the notice’s publication.

Those who fail to appear within the deadline could face further legal action under the Foreign Employment Act, 2007, and other applicable laws, the department said. The measures could include freezing bank accounts used for financial transactions and restricting travel.

In the third week of August, Malaysia selected recruitment agencies from 10 labour-sending countries, including Nepal, to supply workers to the country. It selected 25 Nepali agencies as “principal agencies” and another 250 as “support agencies”.

The Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment directed the department to investigate why Malaysia had selected only 25 principal agencies from Nepal and take action where necessary. The department initially issued arrest warrants against the owners of the principal agencies to obtain their statements.

The agencies had earlier submitted six-point explanations to the department. Officials sought details about why and how the firms had been registered with Malaysia’s Foreign Worker Centralised Management System (FWCMS), the criteria and evaluation methods used to select them, and the process through which they were approved.

The department also asked which authorities had recommended or approved their registration, whether their inclusion in the system restricted competition among Nepali recruitment agencies, and whether any unlawful financial activity had occurred. It further sought clarification on whether the process violated the Foreign Employment Act, 2007, the Foreign Employment Rules, 2008, or other applicable laws.

The department has already halted the issuance of pre-approval for labour permits to the selected agencies until the investigation and legal proceedings are completed.

The agency owners, however, say they are ready to cooperate with the investigation.

“The Labour Ministry has held discussions with us only once. Following that discussion, we also submitted a written request asking that we be removed from Malaysia’s Foreign Worker Centralised Management System through diplomatic channels,” one agency owner told Kantipur. “We have already submitted all the documents the department requested concerning our companies’ transactions. We are ready to cooperate with the investigation.”

On August 22, Malaysia’s Ministry of Human Resources issued a statement announcing a new procedure for recruiting foreign workers. Under the system, Malaysian employers would be allowed to recruit workers only through agencies registered with FWCMS.

The system lists 25 recruitment agencies from Nepal, 99 from the Philippines, 40 each from Sri Lanka and Vietnam, 25 from Bangladesh, 23 from Cambodia, 10 each from India, Myanmar and Pakistan, and one from Thailand.

Nepal has objected to Malaysia’s selection process. Talks between the two countries at prime ministerial and labour ministerial levels have yet to resolve the dispute.

During a telephone conversation with his Malaysian counterpart, Nepal’s Labour Minister Ramjee Yadav urged Malaysia to include all licensed Nepali recruitment agencies in FWCMS and reconsider its selection criteria.

title: Cyclone Arnab prompts three-day nationwide alert as heavy rain and snow loom - The Himalayan Times
description: Cyclone Arnab prompts three-day nationwide alert as heavy rain and snow loom  The Himalayan Times
publisher.title: The Himalayan Times
full_article:
Key Takeaways:

Nepal issues three-day high alert over Cyclone Arnab

Five provinces expected to face the strongest impacts

Heavy snowfall snowstorms and avalanche risks forecast in Himalayan areas

Road air travel and daily activities could face disruptions

Nepal has issued a high-alert advisory for October 29-31 as Cyclone Arnab, expected to make landfall in India, could bring heavy rain, thunderstorms, strong winds and snowfall across large parts of the country.

Related Articles Heavy rain, thunderstorms forecast in several provinces today Windstorms, heavy rain forecast across several provinces

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) warned that the cyclone's impacts are likely to be felt from the night of October 29, with Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini provinces expected to face the greatest effects on October 30 and 31.

Forecasters say moderate rainfall accompanied by thunder, lightning and strong winds is likely in many places, while heavy rainfall is possible in some areas. Karnali and Sudurpashchim provinces could also experience rain and thunderstorms, with isolated heavy downpours.

The authority expressed particular concern for high-hill and Himalayan districts, where heavy snowfall, snowstorms and avalanches are possible. Tourists, trekkers and mountaineers have been urged to avoid travel to high-altitude regions during the alert period, while those already in the mountains have been advised to remain in safe locations.

Authorities also warned of potential disruptions to road transport, flights and daily life, especially near rivers and flood-prone areas. The public has been asked to avoid unnecessary travel and closely follow official forecasts and early-warning updates.

Emergency agencies will remain on standby throughout the three-day period as officials monitor the cyclone's path and its potential impact on Nepal.
